record.body:
## Rationale

The user chose this. One row per requirement matches how assessments and release are decided, keeps rows stable as evidence arrives, and fits a side pane by dropping the least decisive columns first.

## Counter-argument

A per-acceptance grid shows exactly which check is missing for a requirement with several acceptances, which a single latest-check column hides.

payload.alternatives: a requirement x acceptance grid; problems-first ordering; stacking each requirement on two lines in narrow panes
payload.choice: The Evidence tab is one row per requirement in id order (id, text, traced tasks done/total, latest check, status, next), with problem rows coloured; narrow panes drop text, then evidence kind and age
